title: Guards Audit
eyebrow: Audit for approval · GitHub issue 285, "Guards block only unrecoverable actions" · nothing changed yet

short.lead: I went through every hook (an automatic check) in hook.py that can stop me, against your test: only data loss with no way back, or a change to someone else's work, should stop me. Nine kinds of action keep asking or stay refused. Deletes ask only when the data isn't saved. Four refusals become reminders. The background-work guard goes completely. Publishing a page is never refused again.
short.hint: Tap a card for what it guards today and what changes.
key: Still asks you first, or is refused
items: Three things no guard may ever stop

You set these three requirements at 14:45 on 15 October. First, a routine commit or push to an agent-created branch other than main is never blocked. That means a branch named AjsAgent/ or claude/, or a helper's own working-copy branch. Second, publishing an artifact is never blocked. Third, the agent, or a helper it starts, can always change its own files inside the folder it was given. No prompt, refusal or timeout applies to any of them.
Nothing from you. It will be built first and tested by verify.py.
Nine kinds of action that still stop me

Pushing or committing to main (the shared primary branch) stays refused. Commits, merges, rebases, cherry-picks and reverts are now refused too on any branch the guard can't confirm is mine; the refusal tells me to make a new AjsAgent/ branch and commit there. These still ask first: a force-push (overwriting history on the server), a push with --all or --mirror, deleting a branch (local with branch -D, remote with push --delete), git clean (deletes untracked files), and filter-branch (rewrites history). Reset, checkout -- and restore also ask while uncommitted work (changes not yet saved in git) exists. So do stash drop and clear (discarding set-aside work) and truncating (emptying) a file.
Nothing from you. Refusing commits on a branch that isn't clearly mine is stricter than today, which only asks.
Deletes ask only when the file isn't saved

Today every rm asks, even for a committed file git can restore. After this, a delete asks only when it is recursive, meaning it removes a whole folder (rm -r, rmdir /s, Remove-Item -Recurse), or when a file it deletes has uncommitted changes or was never committed. Deleting a committed, unchanged file runs without asking.
Background work and process kills stop asking

These stop asking: background or hidden commands (nohup, a trailing &, Start-Process, background jobs), cutting a wait's output short with tail or head, and killing a process. None of these changes a branch or deletes saved work. The "Never hide work" rule text goes too, along with its 5-minute stall-check reminder.

Each of these is refused today and becomes a reminder. First, publishing a page not built by make_page.py. Second, a Claude credit line or a claude/ branch name on GitHub, and an issue without its sections. Third, a third helper (a sub-agent) running, or a helper starting its own helper. Fourth, overwriting a whole file: today it always asks; afterwards it asks only when that file has uncommitted changes.

Today one unanswered prompt (a question asking for your OK) makes every later prompt in the session refuse at once. That chain of refusals blocked both page publishes and the commit of the automatic-pages page. After this, the timeout only acts on prompts the guards above raise, never on others such as publishing a page. Each prompt waits on its own, and nothing is refused just because an earlier one went unanswered.
The design-loop lock stops code edits until you approve a build plan. It stopped a builder today, but it also makes plans reach you as a page first. Choose in the Choices section below.
Your choice on the design-loop lock.
